title: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties
main_claim: For any abelian variety A/Qbar with good reduction A_0 at w, any rational Hodge class gamma in codimension r, and any divisors D_1..D_{d-r} on A_0, the traces of gamma_0 * c_1(D_1)...c_1(D_{d-r}) agree with a single rational number q in every l-adic realization (l != p) and in crystalline cohomology over C_w, for every p including p=2. As a consequence (using the companion CM Hodge theorem), every specialized Hodge class is represented by a rational algebraic cycle on A_0.

issues.location: Sec. 2, Lemma 2.4 (auxiliary datum), Lemma 2.5 (admissible realization), proof of Prop. 2.1 case (1)
issues.description: The integral-model inputs are used as black boxes and I could not check them against the cited sources offline: Kisin–Zhou 2025 Prop. 2.1.9 and Thm. 2.2.7 (special-point lift in each tensor isogeny class), with p=2 explicitly included; Pappas–Rapoport Thm. 4.10.6 integral uniformization; and Gleason–Lim–Xu Cor. 6.3 as the source of condition (U_x). The paper's verification of the hypotheses (quasi-split J, connected full stabilizer from torsion-free coinvariants, R-smoothness, reduced relative root system at p=2) looks internally consistent. This is residual dependence risk, not a demonstrated gap.
issues.evidence: 'Condition (U_x) holds by [GLX26, Cor 6.3]'; 'All cited global Hodge-type and strongly admissible results apply at p=2 as well.'

issues.location: Lemma 2.5, admissible-locus step ('rho^{-1}(Z_GL) ⊂ Z_J ... puts f_F in F^adm_{J,mu}')
issues.description: The paper concludes that the J-filtration is J-admissible because its GL image is admissible, and justifies this only by citing PR (3.1.9) together with a remark about centers. The step is in fact valid: a G-bundle whose faithful pushforward is trivial is basic with nu=0, and its kappa invariant is fixed by (b,mu) and equals zero. The paper does not spell this out. In the case actually used (the Weil group, whose derived group is simply connected) pi_1(J) is torsion-free anyway.
issues.evidence: Text: 'Since rho is faithful, rho^{-1}(Z_{GL(W)}) ⊂ Z_J ... therefore puts f_F in F^adm_{J,mu}.'

coverage:
I read all of the LaTeX (intro, Sections 1–5) and checked the following steps by hand.
- Lemma 1.3 (pairing property under rational pullback, via rational solving with the Lefschetz Gram matrix).
- Lemma 1.4 (lifting prescribed homomorphisms).
- The CM-transport normalization. Preserving u_psi forces a^*theta_B = lambda_v theta_*. Pairing with theta_*^{D-1} makes lambda_v rational and the same in every realization. Then u_eta gives a^*eta_B = lambda^r f_0^*eta_C. The trace identity j^*f^*eta_C = [P:Q]gamma holds, so kappa = lambda^{-r}/[P:Q] eta_B.
- Theorem 3.1, the u-stable weakly admissible Lagrangian:
  - f = t_H − t_N is supermodular, so there is a unique largest maximizer, and it is E- and u-stable.
  - B(x,y) = beta(x,uy) is alternating and compatible with E and u^2; the blocks M_{tau,z} are B-orthogonal, and B(ux,uy) = zB(x,y).
  - L is beta-Lagrangian of dimension s at each embedding.
  - The slope sum on each block is m, giving t_N(M') >= max(0, a−m).
  - The generic Lagrangian intersection bound and the degree <= m minor bound hold.
  - The Kronecker substitution plus [K_1(theta):K_1] = q > B avoidance argument (q prime, larger than both B and e) works.
- Lemma 4.2 (orthogonality): the eigenspace degree count, the Pi block projection into U⊗Omega, rational density, and the kernel abelian subvariety meeting every eigenspace via the rational characteristic polynomial.
- Lemma 4.3: the coefficient of x_tau^{2s} is D_tau^s, and the annihilator/density argument holds.
- The proof of Prop. 4.1: R_0 f_0 = f_0, q_0 kills ker R_0, and the lifted R, E-action and D are compatible with the support of R^*kappa.
- The CM reduction: the idempotent coordinates (xi = tau rho), U_tau = ⊕_{rho in Delta} V_{tau rho}, the polarization psi⊗Tr(k l̄), and the rational-span descent.
- Circularity check: the companion CM Hodge paper (Oct-6) is used only for Cor. 5.4, and that paper cites this one only in a remark.
I did not verify the external theorems (Kisin–Zhou 2025, Pappas–Rapoport, GLX 2026, Moonen 5.6.3) against their sources.
sibling_notes: The Oct-6 CM Hodge paper (The-rational-Hodge-conjecture-for-CM-abelian-varieties) cites this paper only in Remark 7.x (algebraic specialization), not for its main theorem, so the two do not depend on each other circularly. That remark's locators (Cor 3.4, Cor 6.4) look stale relative to this version's numbering, but that is citation hygiene only.
